mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen for four consecutive weekly means; this self-momentum continues as reopening persists, so mean RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks exceeds the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -72.6 to -41.1 over t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to mean over the last 28 days despite the prior four-week rise.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT crossing above -45 percent change from baseline signals that commuting demand has recovered enough to support non-essential retail trips, lifting RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean rises above -45 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -69.0 to -39.9 by t-0w
failure_condition: After TRANSIT crosses above -45, next 7-day RETAIL_REC mean is not higher than the prior 7-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Joint recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates restored commuting and mobility networks, which jointly increase retail footfall over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -64.0 to -40.6 and TRANSIT from -69.0 to -39.9
failure_condition: When both series improve for two consecutive weeks, next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is lower than last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: As GROCERY_PHARM returns toward baseline, routine essential shopping normalizes and releases time and travel capacity for retail-and-recreation trips over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean rises above -20 percent change from baseline
failure_condition: After GROCERY_PHARM exceeds -20, RETAIL_REC next 14-day mean is not higher than last 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL declining from +24.3 to +12.7 shows people leaving home more; continued decline below +15 predicts higher retail-and-recreation mobility within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below +15 percent change from baseline
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls below +15 but next 14-day RETAIL_REC mean is less than or equal to last 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS recovery and retail recovery interact: as outdoor activity normalizes under eased restrictions, it pulls RETAIL_REC upward over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improves by more than 5 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -68.4 to -46.1 while RETAIL_REC rose from -72.6 to -41.1
failure_condition: When PARKS improves by more than 5 points for two consecutive weeks, next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is lower than last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Monsoon onset in late June typically suppresses outdoor retail and park visits in Delhi; if PARKS declines more than 10 points from its t-0w level, RETAIL_REC will be lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean declines by more than 10 points below -46.1 in any week after 2021-06-22
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at t-0w is -46.1, still below baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next 28-day mean is higher than last 28-day mean even though PARKS declines by more than 10 points below -46.1.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of falling RESIDENTIAL and rising TRANSIT indicates broad out-of-home substitution; when both occur together, retail-and-recreation recovery strengthens over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines week-on-week while TRANSIT rises week-on-week in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 24.3 to 12.7 and TRANSIT rose from -69.0 to -39.9
failure_condition: When RESIDENTIAL declines and TRANSIT rises in the same week, next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is lower than last 28-day mean.
